cases.title: Design a Distributed Unique ID Generator
cases.subtitle: Generate 64-bit strictly monotonic, roughly time-ordered IDs at 100,000+ QPS without central coordination bottlenecks.
functional: IDs must be globally unique 64-bit integers fitting standard database primary keys.
IDs must be roughly sortable by generation time (enabling index locality).
System must generate over 100,000 unique IDs per second with < 2ms latency.
nonFunctional: High availability (99.999% uptime) with zero single point of failure (SPOF).
Clock drift resilience (safe handling of NTP backward time jumps).
deepDives: Twitter Snowflake bit allocation: 1 sign bit + 41-bit millisecond timestamp + 10-bit machine/datacenter ID + 12-bit per-millisecond sequence counter (4,096 IDs/ms per node).
Addressing NTP backward clock drift: If `current_timestamp < last_timestamp`, pause thread until clock catches up or fail over to backup logical sequences.
commonMistakes: Using UUIDv4 (128-bit, non-sequential, severely degrades B-tree index insertion performance).
Using auto-incrementing SQL ID with step offsets (creates tight database coupling and cross-datacenter sync delays).
cases.seniorNotes: At senior staff level, discuss how Snowflake IDs encode the node ID, which could leak datacenter topology or generate rate patterns if exposed raw in client-facing URLs. Mask with Feistel cipher or format-preserving encryption if exposed.

cases.title: Design a Real-Time Collaborative Document Editor
cases.subtitle: Enable multi-user simultaneous document editing with sub-100ms sync and conflict-free convergence.
functional: Multiple authors can edit the same document concurrently in real-time.
Offline editing mode with automatic reconciliation upon network reconnection.
Cursor position and selection presence broadcast to all active collaborators.
nonFunctional: Strong Eventual Consistency (SEC): All connected peers converge to the exact same text without central locking.
deepDives: Operational Transformation (OT) vs Conflict-free Replicated Data Types (CRDT): OT requires a central transformation server (e.g. Google Docs). State-based and operation-based CRDTs (e.g. Yjs, Automerge using RGA trees) allow decentralized peer convergence without central mediation.
Websocket gateway connection tier with Redis Pub/Sub room clustering for broadcast.
commonMistakes: Relying on last-write-wins (LWW) timestamp registers for character streams, which leads to character clipping and lost edits.
cases.seniorNotes: Emphasize garbage collection of deleted character tombstones in CRDT data structures to prevent unbounded memory growth over prolonged collaborative sessions.

cases.title: Design a Global Distributed Rate Limiting Service
cases.subtitle: Enforce per-tenant throughput budgets across distributed API gateways with minimal latency overhead.
functional: Enforce rate limits based on client IP, authenticated User ID, or API Key.
Support multi-tier limits (e.g. 100 req/sec and 50,000 req/day).
Return remaining quota and retry-after headers on HTTP 429.
nonFunctional: Evaluation overhead < 2ms at P99 so upstream API latency is unaffected.
Soft-fail behavior: If rate limiting cluster becomes unreachable, fail open to avoid blackholing traffic.
deepDives: Local gateway token caching with batch synchronization to central Redis cluster to reduce remote round trips.
Sliding window counter algorithm using Redis sorted sets (ZSET) vs Lua script atomic hash maps.
commonMistakes: Executing naive `GET` then `SET` in Redis, causing critical race conditions under concurrent client bursts.
cases.seniorNotes: Address cross-region rate synchronization latency: rather than synchronizing every single token across oceanic links, partition the global quota across regions proportionally to historical regional traffic.
